palettes.statement: The default compatibility palette (the boot ROM's choice for a cartridge that is not Nintendo-licensed or whose title checksum it does not know; 'Right + A' when chosen by hand): four RGB555 colours each, white to black.

dmg_compat.post_boot_b_note: B is the sum of the 16 title bytes when the old licensee code is 0x01 (or 0x33 with new licensee "01"), else 0; HL is 0x991A when that B is 0x43 or 0x58, else 0x007C
dmg_compat.statement: A DMG cartridge (header byte 0x143 without bit 7) on the CGB: the boot ROM writes 0x04 to KEY0 (DMG compatibility mode) and 1 to OPRI (objects by X coordinate), loads the compatibility palettes (OBJ0, OBJ1 through OCPD, then BG through BCPD, with auto-increment) and hands over. The CGB-mode registers then lock: 'locked' ones read 0xFF and ignore writes, 'read-only' ones keep their value and ignore writes; the rest (BCPS/OCPS, FF72, FF73, FF75, PCM12/34) work as in CGB mode. The PPU draws the DMG way (no attributes, bank 0, LCDC bit 0 blanks the background) with BGP/OBP0/OBP1 indexing the CGB palettes BG 0 and OBJ 0/1.

registers.name: KEY0
registers.note: written by the boot ROM only (the header's CGB flag when its bit 7 is set, else 0x04: bit 2 = DMG compatibility mode) and locked by its write to FF50; reads 0xFF afterwards

sources: Gekkio, Game Boy: Complete Technical Reference
statement: Game Boy Color registers: KEY0 (the boot ROM's mode choice), double speed (KEY1 + STOP), VRAM and WRAM banks, colour palettes, object priority mode, undocumented FF72-FF75; DMG compatibility mode for DMG cartridges (dmg_compat).
